summary: The note defines ethical hedonism as the idea that people have the right to pursue the greatest amount of pleasure possible for them, and that a person's pleasure should far exceed their pain. It attributes the origin of the view to Aristippus of Cyrene, described as a student of Socrates, who held that pleasure is the highest good. The note is very short and covers only the basic definition and its origin.
one_line: Defines ethical hedonism as the pursuit of maximum personal pleasure, traced to Aristippus of Cyrene, a student of Socrates.
key_facts: Ethical hedonism is the idea that all people have the right to do everything in their power to achieve the greatest amount of pleasure possible to them.
Ethical hedonism holds that every person's pleasure should far surpass their amount of pain.
Ethical hedonism is said to have been started by Aristippus of Cyrene.
Aristippus of Cyrene is described in the note as a student of Socrates.
Aristippus of Cyrene held the idea that pleasure is the highest good.
